name: Clark County Treasurer
notes: Researched 2026-10-10 from public clarkcountynv.gov Treasurer pages only (no sign-in, no lookup). Pay online through Treasurer Web (e-check free; debit/credit Visa, MasterCard, Discover with a third-party service fee whose amount is not published, so no card fee is charged in the mock), by the automated phone system (702) 455-4323 option 1 (e-check or card), by mail with the coupon (Box 551220, Las Vegas, NV 89155-1220), drop box, kiosk or in person Mon-Thu 7:30-5:30. Taxes are due the third Monday in August, or in four installments (3rd Monday Aug, 1st Monday Oct, Jan, Mar) when over $100; 10-day grace; penalty 4% for one late installment rising to 22% for the oldest of four. Unpaid on the first Monday in June starts a two-year redemption period at 10%/yr. Bills are mailed once a year; duplicate bills by phone option 3 or online. No paperless bill or automatic payment program is described (tax reminders sign-up exists but its content is not public), so both are unsupported (inferred). Email sign-in is synthetic.

help.title: Real property tax payment options
paragraphs: Online, pay by e-check with no fee, or by debit or credit card (Visa, MasterCard or Discover) with a service fee charged by the third-party provider.

By phone, call the automated system at (702) 455-4323 and choose option 1; e-check, debit and credit cards are accepted. By mail, make the check payable to Clark County Treasurer, write your parcel number on it, include the payment coupon, and send it to 500 S Grand Central Pkwy, Box 551220, Las Vegas, NV 89155-1220.

In person, the office at 500 S Grand Central Pkwy (first floor) is open Monday to Thursday, 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., and takes cash, checks and debit cards with no fee. A kiosk and a drop box for checks are also at the Government Center, and you can add Clark County Treasurer as a payee in your bank's bill pay.

help.title: Due dates and penalties
paragraphs: Taxes are due the third Monday in August. If they are over $100, you may pay in four installments instead (not quarterly): the third Monday in August, and the first Mondays in October, January and March.

Each payment must be made within 10 days of its due date. One late installment adds a 4% penalty; with more late installments the penalty on each grows, up to 22% on the oldest when all four are late. Taxes unpaid at the end of April are advertised as delinquent, and if still unpaid on the first Monday in June the property enters a two-year redemption period with 10% annual interest.

help.title: Getting your tax bill
paragraphs: Real property tax bills are mailed only once each fiscal year. If yours has not arrived by August 1, request a copy through the automated phone system or online; copies go to the mailing address on record. If you bought the property during the year, or your mortgage company stopped paying, call (702) 455-4323, option 3.
Not receiving a bill does not excuse late payment or remove penalties. If your mortgage company pays from escrow, write your loan number on the bill and send it to them.
